summary: Meera asks whether she can take a car loan with a Rs 9,000 EMI. FOIR allows it; her 42% card says wait.
split_note: Discovery (D53): v1's traces on this task are where prompt v2's changes may come from.

messages.content: I'm thinking of buying a car with a loan. The EMI would be about ₹9,000. Can I afford it?

graders.description: Floor only: the card is mentioned. Whether it is recommended first is the judge's criterion.

The judge (rubric advice.v1, D68): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the answer recommend clearing the 42% credit card (₹84,250) before taking on the car loan? Yes or no.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

Whether the car is affordable hinges on the down payment she plans to make, which neither she nor her records give. Does the advisor ask for it, or say which down payment it assumed and how the answer would change? Yes or no.

judge_criteria_to_write: Judgment (R6 crux): FOIR room is 32130.00 a month, so the EMI fits, but a good advisor says clear the 42% card first. Expected: affordable on paper, not advisable yet.
